# NOTES: coa12, the Companies Act 2006 (United Kingdom), Part 16 (Audit), Chapters 3 to 7: ss 495 to 539 (lines 6970-7555)

**Status (generated by `work/build-notes.py` from the files in this folder on the day the check below was run):** layer 1 (`coa12-ch3a-report`, `-ch3b-rights`, `-ch4a-removal`, `-ch4b-resignation`, `-ch5-concerns`, `-ch6-liability`, `-ch7-definitions`, helpers `coa12-logic`), their tests, and the seat layer are written and checked on the two stable builds; see "What check.sh prints" for the numbers. Nothing here has been read by a lawyer; every reading that a lawyer should overrule is in the fork register or in "Marginal readings for a lawyer". Nothing is "verified against the official text".

## About this text and this note

- **The text is a converter rendering, not the official text.**
  `inputs/ukpga-2006-46.txt` is a plain-text rendering of the Act made from legislation.gov.uk by a converter script (Open Government Licence v3.0; `inputs/SOURCES.md`).
  Nothing here is "verified against the official text".
  Every `-- src:N | ...` quotation in the `.l4` files is copied by `work/gen.py` from that file, line by line, and `srcrefs.py` checks each quotation and each `@ref` locator against it (counts below).
  Where the rendering looks damaged (dots where words were omitted, a missing subsection, a stray quotation mark, two paragraphs lettered (a)) the finding is recorded in "What the text turns out to say", and the encoding follows the words as rendered.
- **The seat is assumed, not ruled.**
  The seat is the brief's: an individual who is, or is about to become, a director, a company secretary or a member of a company registered under the Act, or who deals with one.
  The brief marks it "(Assumed, not ruled: the Act is addressed to companies, so the individual is whoever stands in a company's management or ownership.)".
  A second assumption of mine, also assumed and not ruled: the individual auditor (and an officer or employee of an auditor) is "who deals with" the company, so the seat has questions in the auditor's voice (each says so in its comment).
  There is never a seat for an official: ss 508, 509 and 524 address only officials and have no seat question; layer 1 records what they decide.
- **Where the brief and PLAN.md differ, the brief governs (and this is where they differ).**
  1. Imports. The brief says layer 1 IMPORTs the keel's `coa-core.l4` and `coa-definitions.l4`; PLAN.md section 1 step 2 and section 4.1 say a part imports `prelude`, `daydate` and `coa-core`, and that "Parts cannot import the keel's definitions module" but take each keel answer as an INPUT.
     The brief governs: every layer-1 module `coa12-ch*` imports both keel modules (probed on 1.6.110 and 1.6.109 on 2026-11-13: no diagnostics, every assertion unchanged).
     The keel answers (`s 4(1) the company is a private company`, `s 1173(1) ... is a parent company`, ...) are still taken as INPUTS named for the keel function, as PLAN.md 4.1 names them, so the lead can wire them at the merge; no keel function is called.
  2. The brief says seam inputs are "as PLAN.md section 8 names it"; PLAN.md has no section 8. The seam names come from PLAN.md 4.1, 4.2 and my row of section 6 (see "Seams (coa12)").
  3. The brief says every top-level name begins with its provision's section label.
     The shared helpers in `coa12-logic.l4` are not a provision, so they begin `coa12 ` (the part id), which no other part can use; the seat helpers begin `coa12 seat`.
     The seat questions begin "Under section N," as the brief's seat rule requires, not `s N`.
- **The rulings that govern the `FALSE` and `NOTHING` tags are reproduced word for word** in "Fork register (coa12)" (E1, N2, the 2026-11-05 rulings and the case-by-case ruling), because this part uses `NOTHING-kind` tags in every module.
- **Where the code is.**
  The `.l4` files in this folder are generated from templates by `work/gen.py` (the quotation lines and `@ref` locators are copied mechanically from the text) and, for the seat files, by `work/seatgen.py`; `work/build.sh` regenerates, runs `srcrefs.py` in both modes, runs `check.sh` against both builds, and regenerates this note.
  Only the files in this folder are the deliverable; `work/` is scratch.

## Fork register (coa12)

Every ambiguity of this part, the readings seen, the one taken and the text that licenses each. The rulings that govern the `FALSE` and `NOTHING` tags follow, word for word from the brief, because this part uses `NOTHING-kind` tags in every module.

### The rulings (reproduced word for word from the brief)

- **E1** (bench `commons-negation-1030`; should a legal effect be one definition gathered from every section that gives it?): option B, as guidance for gathering a legal effect's routes by hand only, with no pilot run; option A (gathering by bare name) is withdrawn as a direction for the language, not deferred; option C (per-section answers) applies everywhere else; the Magna Carta pilot in the printed recommendation (chapters 2, 3, 4, 5, 37, 43, 46 and 53, with a blind second reader) is not to be run. The maintainer's lean, verbatim: "B but generally uncomfortable with this much magic because it takes the language from unopinionated to opinionated in ways that are hard to teach an l4 novice." the maintainer's note, verbatim: "Fundamentally I feel like we are trying to make the language do work that the human l4 drafter should do. Too much magic. Can’t we just decline to be this opinionated and say the programmer needs to do this thinking?" Marked 2026-11-03T23:19:02.812Z, ruled 2026-11-04. Bench: https://claude.ai/artifact/49q6k2H5xtuJqy5ttkwZ23

- **N2** (bench `commons-negation-1030`; does a flat negative count as the text's no?): option A as printed: flat negatives count as a no, and where the text names the bearer the prohibition (`SHANT`) is derived from that answer; the Hohfeld kinds stay in each row's "Jural relations" table; option C's wording (the kind typed in the person-facing answer) comes only after a lawyer confirms the typing, decided together with the S/E choice for how "not covered" is said. The maintainer's lean, verbatim: "Why are we even trying to do this work? Some of these rules are metatextual and require more homoiconicity than we currently have in L4." the maintainer's note: none written. Marked 2026-11-03T23:22:49.971Z, ruled 2026-11-04. Bench: https://claude.ai/artifact/49q6k2H5xtuJqy5ttkwZ23

- **Periods, "where" and scope limits** (a question raised on 2026-11-05 while checking an encoding of the Retirement and Re-employment Act 1993, not a bench): (a) a period the text fixes in its own words ("within one month", "begins from ... until the employee attains the age", "on the last day of employment"): outside the period the answer is `JUST FALSE`; (b) a "where ..." condition: when it fails the answer is `JUST FALSE`; (c) a scope limit with no "only" (for example "below" the minimum age): outside the scope the answer is `NOTHING`. The maintainer's words, verbatim apart from the trigger word that ended the message: "i agree with your lean: no for a and b; nothing for c." Typed 2026-11-05T04:30:00.322Z, ruled 2026-11-05.

- **Delegated definitions, defences and "until" bars** (questions raised on 2026-11-05 while checking encodings of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002, the Terrorism Act 2000 and the Singapore Sale of Goods Act 1979, not a bench): (a) a definition the text itself hands to a list ("Schedule 9 has effect for determining what is a business in the regulated sector"): when no head in the list holds, the answer is `JUST FALSE`; a bare list with no such hand-off still answers `NOTHING`; (b) "it is a defence ... to prove that X": when X is not proved, the answer is `JUST FALSE` for that provision's defence, worded "this section gives no defence on these facts" and never "no defence at all"; (c) "when", "upon" and "whenever" count as "where" under rule (b) of the periods ruling above; (d) "the property does not pass until X": encode the bar ("the property cannot yet pass": `JUST TRUE` before X, `JUST FALSE` after X) and never claim that the property has passed. The maintainer approved these four readings as put to him by the general-manager session, in the word NOTHINGBURGER; his note on (d), verbatim apart from the bracket and the trigger word that ended the message: "in the case of Q5 [the "until" bar] i hope we are using the deontic mechanisms to examine a trace." The note is a request about how (d) is modelled, not part of the ruling. Typed 2026-11-05T06:04:54.553Z, ruled 2026-11-05.

- **Questions with no convention: decide case by case (the maintainer, typed 2026-11-05T10:25:24Z).** Six questions the rulings above leave open are decided site by site, at encoding time, on the text's own words and the encoder's best judgment: an "unless" or "except" once it is met; a bare "must" not done; "listed in Schedule N"; a duty whose "if" or "where" is unmet; "(other than X)"; a missing event in the state ledger. Each such site gets one fork line (the provision, the function, the answer taken, the other reading) for the human reviewer to overrule, and the rulings above still govern whatever they cover. The maintainer's words, asked of the session "Encodings": "re Encoding Conventions I believe I had a short discussion with the coordinator where I basically said I agreed with its \"lean\"s -- does that mean we can retire the bench card or should I go over it still? In short I feel like these decisions need to be made case-by-case at encoding time, and you should go with your gut most of the time; and if the encoding turns out to be wrong, well, that's where the human review comes in." The bench that carried the six questions ("Encoding Conventions", artifact Hpg2k9HqExJN5zdtBYiJ72, collection `encodings-conventions-1105`) was retired unmarked, so it holds no marks.

### Named for a grant or a power: listed, not flipped (assumed, not ruled)

The sweep of 2026-11-12 does not flip two groups; they are listed here, one row per function. It is **assumed, not ruled** that "where", "when", "upon" and their equivalents ("in the case of", "so long as", "while", "on payment", "on such an application", "after ...", "before ...", "within ... after ...") go with the first group. Ruling (b) of the Guide's "Periods, where and scope limits" paragraph (and ruling (c) of the 2026-11-05 delegated ruling) says `JUST FALSE` for a failed "where", and the Guide's line on grants points the other way (`NOTHING`); that is a question for the maintainer or a lawyer, not one settled by the sweep. An "entitled" function is a claim, not a power, and the Guide does not settle it.

## Jural relations (coa12)

One row per provision, as the brief asks: the party holding the right (a claim), privilege (a liberty), power or immunity, the party bearing the correlative duty, no-right, liability (being subject to the power) or disability, the section, and the L4 rule that encodes it. Each relation is stated once, neutrally, never from both sides. A provision that creates no such relation (a definition, a counting rule, a blank or a machinery provision) is listed once as `none`. The rows are in text order and cover every section from s 495 to s 539; the L4 names are read from the coverage table.

## Marginal readings for a lawyer (coa12)

The brief marks two readings "for a lawyer": (a) a failed "if" counts as the text's no, clause by clause, within the provision that holds the "if" (an inference: "if A then B" does not itself say "if not A then not B"), and flat negatives count as the text saying no; (b) a prohibition or grant limited by its own wording does not (the case outside the limit answers `NOTHING`). Both are taken as the status quo. This section lists every branch of this part that rests on one of them, with the other reading; it is generated from the `FALSE-kind` and `NOTHING-kind` comments in the layer-1 modules, so a branch with such a comment cannot be missing. A `JUST FALSE` that rests only on a definition by "means" is not marginal and is not listed (the other tables of this note count it).

### Reading a result: FALSE and NOTHING (coa12)

The rule of 2026-10-29 (assumed, not ruled by a lawyer) and the rulings of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05, as they read in this subject.
Every decision function answers `MAYBE BOOLEAN` unless its name says it returns a number, a date, a list or a penalty.

- `JUST TRUE`: the Act says yes.
  In a function named as a bar or a negative (`s 510(4) the auditor is barred from removal before the expiration of his term of office`, `s 516(2) the notice of resignation is not effective`, `s 514(8) the resolution is ineffective`, `s 532(2) the provision is void`) `JUST TRUE` means the bar applies, the notice does not take effect, the provision is void.
- `JUST FALSE` ("a no"): the Act says no in its own words.
  In this part that is one of five things, and each branch carries `-- FALSE-kind (the text says no in its own words): "<the quoted words>"`:
  1. a DUTY function ("must ...") whose own "where", "if" or "on receipt" trigger is unmet: "the section does not oblige the party on these facts" (fork F1), which is not "the party may ignore it";
  2. a CONTENT function ("the report includes what the subsection requires") where a required item is missing: "this item does not meet the requirement" (fork F2), which is not "this is not an auditor's report";
  3. a "means", "are" or "is" definition applied to a case outside it ("liability limitation agreement", "principal terms", "public interest company"; forks F3, F5);
  4. a period or "where" condition the text fixes in its own words, missed (the 2026-11-05 rulings (a) and (b)): the 14 days of s 519(4), the 21 days of s 518(5), the 28 days of s 523(3);
  5. a flat negative ("may not", "is not required", "is not subject", "not void") and an "unless" or "except" once met (N2; fork F6).
- `NOTHING` ("not covered"): the Act does not decide the case.
  In this part that is, for example: s 527(1) for a company that is not quoted (the power is given to "the members of a quoted company" and the section says nothing of another company); s 499(3) when the proceedings are a prosecution under s 501 (the bar lifts, and nothing is granted); a grant named "may" whose plain "if" gate fails (s 506(1), s 511A(2) to (5), s 526: the text does not say the grant is refused; fork F16); every amount, rate or rule the Act leaves to regulations (the terms of a liability limitation agreement under s 535(2); the disclosure under s 538), which are INPUTS; the "fair and reasonable" amount of s 537, which is the court's judgment and an INPUT; the pound values of "the statutory maximum" and "level 3 on the standard scale", which the Act does not state and which are INPUTS; and any answer that rests on a seam input whose own answer is `NOTHING` (the other part's "not covered" stays "not covered": `-- NOTHING-kind (points outside the text)`).
  Each such branch carries `-- NOTHING-kind (<why>)`, <why> being one of silent, list not closed, includes, undefined term, points outside the text, limited by its own wording.
- A caller must never turn `NOTHING` into `FALSE`.
  `REFUSE` is not used; "not covered" is `NOTHING`, asserted in the tests.
- A borrowed term (handed to another Act or instrument) is an input: its `JUST FALSE` is the other instrument's no, supplied by the caller, and its `NOTHING` means the caller does not know it (fork F4).
- Not every function is `MAYBE BOOLEAN`.
  `s 537(2) the amount to which the auditor's liability is limited` and `s 539 the turnover of the company` return a `NUMBER` (the arithmetic has no "not covered");
  `s 516(3) the day on which the auditor's term of office ends` returns `MAYBE DATE`;
  `s 525(1) the appropriate audit authority` returns `MAYBE (LIST OF ...)`;
  each penalty function returns `MAYBE Penalty` (`NOTHING` where the section states no penalty for that mode of conviction).
- In the seat layer a yes/no fact the person states is passed to layer 1 as `JUST TRUE` or `JUST FALSE`, so the seat never answers `NOTHING` because of a fact it asked; a seat `NOTHING` always means the Act is silent on the case.

In this part the text does not answer, among others:

- who is a "non-public interest company": s 519A's heading names it and its body never defines it (fork F10);
- the content of the regulations the Secretary of State may make under s 535(2) (what a liability limitation agreement must or must not contain) and under s 538 (the disclosure), and the pound values of "the statutory maximum" and "level 3 on the standard scale" (inputs);
- the "fair and reasonable" amount of s 537, which is the court's judgment (an input);
- the content of every borrowed term (an issuer under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000; eligibility for appointment as auditor under Part 42; "in default" under s 1121; a quoted, small or micro-entity company under Part 15; ordinary and special resolutions under Part 13): inputs, and `NOTHING` where the caller does not know them;
- what happens to an auditor's report that lacks a required item (s 495(4)(c) and (d) say it "must include" the item; no section says what the report is without it) and to a removal or resignation that does not follow the section: the offence sections (ss 501, 505, 507, 518(6), 519(5), 520(6), 521(3), 522(5), 523(4), 530) are the only consequences the text states;
- who decides, in s 525(1), when both paragraphs (a) apply (fork F8), and what became of s 522(2) to (4) (finding 1);
- what a provision "wholly attributable to circumstances that it would not be reasonable to have expected the company to prevent or avoid" (s 528(5)) requires: an input.

## What the text turns out to say (coa12)

Each finding was read off the text (line numbers are of `ukpga-2006-46.txt`) or off a failing assertion; none rests on memory.

1. **s 522 skips from subsection (1) to subsection (5).**
   Lines 7363 and 7364 are "(1) Where an auditor of a company sends a statement under section 519, ..." and "(5) A person ceasing to hold office as auditor who fails to comply with this section commits an offence."; subsections (2) to (4) are not in the text and, unlike s 524(3) and s 525(2) and (3), no line of dots marks the gap.
   The rendering does not say whether they were repealed or lost by the converter.
   Nothing is encoded for them (there is no text to encode); the coverage table has no row for them because the text has no line for them.
2. **s 525(1) shows two paragraphs lettered (a).**
   Lines 7404 and 7407 both begin "(a)": the first is about "an auditor of a public interest company (other than an Auditor General)" with limbs (i) and (ii); the second is "in the case of a major audit (other than one conducted by an Auditor General), the Financial Reporting Council Limited".
   Both are encoded; the answer is a list (fork F8).
3. **s 519A's heading names "non-public interest company" and its body never defines it.**
   The body defines "public interest company" and "exempt reasons" only (subsection (1) and (3)); sections 516 to 523 use "non-public interest company" as if it were defined (fork F10).
4. **s 507(2)(c) describes s 498(5) wrongly.**
   Line 7136 reads "(c) section 498(5) (statement that directors wrongly took advantage of exemption from obligation to prepare group accounts)."; s 498(5) (lines 7040 to 7044) is about directors who "have prepared accounts in accordance with the small companies regime" or "have taken advantage of small companies exemption from the requirement to prepare a strategic report or in preparing the directors' report".
   The encoding follows the operative words ("a statement required by section 498(5)") and not the parenthetical.
5. **The rendering shows omission dots, a run-together word and a stray mark.**
   Words omitted by amendment appear as dots inside a sentence at lines 6987 (s 495(3)(c), "this Act ...."), 7010 (s 497(1), "a quoted company ..."), 7029 (s 498(1)(c)), 7033 (s 498(2)(c)), 7103 (s 504(1)(b), "... any relevant guidance"), 7402 (the heading of s 525), 7547 (s 539 "MiFID investment firm" (a)) and 7242 (s 515(3), "notice of ... an intended resolutionmentioned in subsection (1)": two words run together).
   Line 7218 (s 514(2A)) ends with a stray closing quotation mark.
   Blank (dots-only) subsections, paragraphs and sections: s 497(3), s 498(7), s 504(1)(a), s 511A(7), s 512, s 517, s 524(3), s 525(2), s 525(3), s 538A(2), two lines inside s 519A(2) (lines 7318 and 7319) and the line after "e-money issuer" in s 539 (line 7545): each is a coverage row "repealed or blank" and the text shows nothing more.
6. **s 495(4)(a) cannot fail.**
   "The auditor's report must be either unqualified or qualified" and s 539 defines "qualified" as a report that "does not state the auditor's unqualified opinion ...", so every report is one or the other.
   `s 495(4)(a) the report is either unqualified or qualified` answers `JUST TRUE` for either answer of `s 539 the report or statement is qualified` and `NOTHING` only where that answer is unknown; the test of this paragraph asserts exactly that.
7. **s 282(5), outside this part, changes the reading of s 510(2) (fork F7).**
   Line 3736 reads "Anything that may be done by ordinary resolution may also be done by special resolution.", so the "ordinary resolution at a meeting" that s 510(2)(a) requires is also satisfied by a special resolution.
8. **A failing assertion was found and fixed in the code, not in the expected value.**
   The first run of `coa12-tests-ch3b` failed 2 of 187 assertions (s 499(1)(b) and s 505(1)).
   Cause: an unbracketed `NOT a OR NOT b` is read by the stable binary as `NOT (a OR NOT b)` (see "What the stable binary does not accept"); every `NOT` in the sources was then bracketed, and the two expected values, written by hand from the text before the run, were not edited.
9. **s 518(5) packs two periods into one sentence (fork F11).**
   "must within 21 days from the date on which the company receives a requisition proceed duly to convene a meeting for a day not more than 28 days after the date of the notice convening the meeting" gives a period for convening and a period from notice to meeting; the encoding tests both periods in one function and carries the 21 days in the deontic rule.
10. **s 528(4)(a) counts working days; s 529(3) fixes an hour.**
    The three days of s 528(4)(a) are working days, so the deontic rule's clock is read in working days and the number of working days is an input (the keel's `s 1173(1)` seam), and s 529(3) ("not later than the time when it makes the statement available") is about the moment of day, not the date: the encoding carries a date and an hour (a comparison of two DATETIME values did not check on either build).

## What the stable binary does not accept (coa12)

Measured on 2026-11-13 by running the files of this part with `L4_BIN` (1.6.110, main, e51181d) and `L4_MAIN` (1.6.109); every result below was the same on both builds.
The binary governs, so the modules use none of the rejected constructs.

**Rejected, loudly (an error or a failed check; the symptom teaches).**

- `APPEND` on a list is a type error (`APPEND` is for strings); the list function is `append`.
- `JUST (append` with its argument continued on the following lines is a parse error; write `JUST` alone and put the argument on its own indented lines.
- `(EMPTY OF T)` fails with "not a function" in a test; write `EMPTY`.
- A field access of a backticked name as an argument (`` `f` reason's `x` ``) does not parse; bracket it: `` `f` (reason's `x`) ``.
- A comparison of two `DATETIME` values did not check on either build even with the datetime and time imports; s 529(3) uses a `DATE` and an hour (a record `s 529(3) time`).
- A `DEONTIC` value cannot be put in an `#ASSERT`: its outcome is READ from `#TRACE`; every duty is therefore encoded twice, as a decision function that carries the assertions and as a deontic rule that is run.
  A `MAY` rule takes no `LEST`.
- `WAIT UNTIL` is spelled `WAITUNTIL`.

**Silent (exit code 0, a wrong answer, caught only because the expected values were written by hand first).**

- An unbracketed `NOT` binds over the whole expression that follows it: `NOT a OR b` is read as `NOT (a OR b)`, and `NOT a OR NOT b` as `NOT (a OR NOT b)`.
  It produced two failures in the first run of `coa12-tests-ch3b` (finding 8); every `NOT` in the sources is bracketed.

**What `check.sh` cannot see.**
`check.sh` compares the four counts of each module between the two builds; it does not see a different `#TRACE` outcome.
`work/tracediff.sh` runs every test file (they carry the `#TRACE`s), the seat cases and the two modules that carry the deontic rules (`coa12-ch4b-resignation`, `coa12-ch5-concerns`) on both builds and compares the complete output, traces included; the result is printed under "What check.sh prints" (identical for each of the nine files when this note was built).
The traces themselves are read, not asserted: `#TRACE` of the s 528(4)(a) rule at day 3 prints `FULFILLED`, at `WAITUNTIL 4` prints `BREACH` with the rule's `BECAUSE` text, and the s 529(3) rule prints `FULFILLED` when the statement is forwarded.

**Accepted and relied on (measured).**
A literal string or party in a deontic action constrains the match on both builds, so a trace that fulfils or breaches is not vacuous; `ROR` works; import diamonds work (several modules import `coa12-logic`, `coa12-ch7-definitions` and the keel); `append`, `Date d m y`, `PLUS` and `MINUS` on dates and comparisons on dates work; `Penalty` values can be constructed and compared; and a `§` heading before a declaration is accepted.
`REFUSE`, `#ASSERT REFUSED`, `YMD`, sets and `TYPICALLY` are not used.

## The seat layer (coa12)

`coa12-seat.l4` and `coa12-cases-seat.l4` are generated from one specification (`work/seatgen.py`): each question calls a layer-1 rule and restates none; its inputs are plain facts, one per fact the person can state, each with an `@desc` worded as that person would be asked; the questions are grouped under `§` headings in text order; every question has `@export`, and every name begins "Under section N,". The seat is **assumed, not ruled** (see "About this text and this note").

73 questions and 167 cases in the case file (expected values typed in `work/seatgen.py` from the text before any run). Every question has at least one case; 24 questions have a case whose expected answer is `NOTHING` (not covered), asserted.

### Seat questions: name and direction (the audit the brief asks for)

**First pass (the brief's self-audit, reading each name against its own title).** Two of the 73 questions differed and were fixed at the time: section 510(4) (it asked about the company where the function is the bar on the auditor's removal) and section 527(5) (it asked "even though the court may find the rights are being abused", which the body does not).

**Second pass of 2026-11-12 (reading each name and `@export` text against the BODY of the layer-1 function it calls).** 73 questions read; **26** retitled (direction: 0; subject: 26), the rest unchanged. The rule applied: a name may carry the provision's subject (the conduct an offence section describes, the thing a section is about, the limb it answers), but may not state as given a fact the function tests as a separate input (a status such as "a firm", "a general meeting", "removed", "public interest company", "written resolution"), and may not ask more or less than the one limb the body answers. The bars and negatives were checked in the direction of their layer-1 function (ss 499(3), 499(4), 504(3), 510(4), 514(8), 516(2), 527(5), 529(2), 532(2)); none was a negation of a permission. Nothing in a body changed because of a retitle; the case file carries the new names, and each assertion whose name changed has a `RECONCILED 2026-11-12` comment above it giving the old name. The questions kept as they were include the offence questions that name the offence by its conduct (ss 501(1), 501(3), 505(3), 507(1), 518(6), 520(6), 530(1)): there the conduct is the offence's description and not a separate fact the function tests as a status.

## Tests (coa12)

Expected values are written beside each assertion, decided from the text before the run; none is copied from the encoding's output. Every layer-1 module has a test file (`coa12-tests-ch3a`, `-ch3b`, `-ch4a`, `-ch4b`, `-ch5`, `-ch6`); `coa12-ch7-definitions` and `coa12-logic` are exercised through them. Every one of the layer-1 functions is named in a test file or in the seat cases (`work/build-notes.py` computes the list of any that is not and fails if there is one); the tests were written to take each branch and each side of every threshold or period (the last day and the day after), with not-covered cases asserted `NOTHING`; branch coverage is not measured by a tool. The deontic rules are run with `#TRACE` (their outcome is read, not asserted; see "What the stable binary does not accept"), and each is paired with a decision function whose assertions carry the same cases. No assertion is meant to fail; `expected_failed` in `check.sh` is empty.

Layer-1 functions: 277; named in a test file or called by a seat question: 277.

The FALSE/NOTHING tag audit (`work/audit.py`, run when this note was built): 214 `JUST FALSE` result branches and 161 `NOTHING` result branches in the layer-1 modules, **0** without their `FALSE-kind` or `NOTHING-kind` comment (the three-valued connectives in `coa12-logic.l4` are exempt: they read nothing from the text).
